column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health.
Ship `/app/run.json` and serve the workspace and API on one port with a health endpoint, as specified in Deployment.

Seeded sign-in.
Seeded people sign in with email and password and receive a session that every other API call and screen requires, as specified in API.

Project isolation.
A person can list, promote and read evidence only in projects they belong to, and other projects' stages, bundles and promotions answer as unknown.

Role checks on the server.
Every action in the authority table in Business rules is refused by the server for a project role that may not perform it, whatever the screen shows.

One error shape and precedence.
Every error response except the health endpoint's starting answer uses the single error body and the single precedence order stated in API.

Same-origin boundary.
The server accepts state-changing browser calls only from its own origin, enforces the content type and body limits, and never serves source, configuration or credentials, as specified in Server boundary.

Credentials from the environment.
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and never reaches the browser or the source tree.

Boot with dependencies down.
The server starts and reports healthy while object storage or mail is unreachable, and every feature that does not need the missing service keeps working, as qualified in Services.

Status by glyph and label.
Every stage and resource status shows a glyph and a visible word as well as a colour, at the contrast levels in Visual design.

Three viewports.
The workspace fits 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 without horizontal scrolling, and the stage graph stacks vertically when the viewport is narrower than 768 pixels.

Keyboard and touch operation.
Every public control works by keyboard with a visible focus ring and the Tab, Enter and Escape behaviour in Interactions, and by touch at the target size in Visual design.

Nocturnal instrument look.
The workspace uses the graphite ground, amber accent, typefaces and tabular numerals described in Visual design.

Rail, graph and evidence composition.
The workspace is composed as a left rail, a stage graph with a ledger strip pinned beneath it, and a right evidence column, as described in Screens and layout.

Reduced-motion rail.
With reduced motion requested, the rail shows five labelled segments that fill at once, counters change without counting, and the progress live region announces every phase.

Motion only on state change.
Nothing on screen moves unless server state changed or the user acted, and no decorative loop runs while the workspace is idle.

Announced feedback.
Every async action shows its pending, success, error and outage copy from Feedback states in the named live regions.

Server-driven rail.
The rail's phase, progress and counter come from server-reported promotion state, never from a client timer or a client-side estimate.

Ingest release bundles.
A bundle ingest stores the rendered manifests in object storage under the SHA-256 digest of the stored bytes before it answers, and returns that digest.

Bundle validation.
Malformed manifests, duplicate resources, duplicate versions and oversized bodies are rejected with the statuses in API and leave no record and no object behind.

Bundle ready to promote.
A bundle ingested by the build pipeline appears in the dev stage's Promote dialog within the refresh delay in Interactions, with its version and short digest.

Request a promotion.
A promotion request records the bundle, the stage defaults merged with request overrides, the requester, the request instant and the freeze policy version in force, and non-prod requests run the window check at once.

Promote only verified bundles.
A bundle may enter a stage only after it has reached Healthy in that stage's upstream stage.

Retries return the original result.
A repeated promote, approve, reject, start, re-check, freeze-break or rollback call with the same request key and body returns the original response, and the same key with a different body is refused.

Promote to staging from the graph.
A service developer promotes a dev-healthy bundle to staging from the evidence column, and a double press on the confirm button still creates exactly one promotion.

Cluster agent reports.
The cluster sync agent's per-resource reports move a running promotion from applying to health wait to Healthy or Degraded by the rules in Business rules.

In-sync counter equals health rows.
Every "in sync n/N" value on screen and in the API equals the Synced-and-Healthy rows and the total rows for the stage's current revision.

Rail phase and progress attributes.
Each rail edge exposes data-phase and data-progress equal to the server's phase and progress for that edge within the refresh delay in Interactions.

Promotion rail motion.
A capsule with the short digest advances along the edge whenever the server-reported progress rises and never moves backward, the counter counts up to each new value, the target border flashes once on Healthy, and on failure the drawn segment turns red from the capsule back to the source.

Watch a promotion reach Healthy.
A service developer watches a promotion move from Queued to Healthy on the rail as agent reports arrive, without reloading the page.

One active promotion per stage.
Of simultaneous promotion requests to one stage exactly one wins, and every other request is refused with the name of the bundle that holds the stage.

Told who holds the stage.
A developer who loses the race for prod-eu sees which bundle holds the stage, and the graph shows prod-eu as Out-of-sync with the winner's digest.

Approval requested mail.
A prod promotion request sends one approval-requested message to every release manager of the project, carrying a link that works while the request is pending, until it is decided or expires.

Approve or reject a prod promotion.
Only a release manager may approve or reject a promotion that awaits approval, and approval is refused until the request's evidence snapshot is stored.

Approval is all or nothing.
An approval records the decision, stores a new evidence snapshot and records the requester's notice together, and when storage fails none of them exists.

Approve with the evidence in view.
A release manager follows the approval link, signs in, reviews the redacted diff and the stage's live health rows in the evidence column and approves, and the requester receives the approved notice.

Server-side approval lifetime.
A prod promotion may start only before its approval's expiry instant, which is excluded, and a start at or after it is refused and marks the promotion expired.

One expiry notice.
A request or approval that lapses is marked expired by the server within the sweep delay in Business rules and sends exactly one expiry notice to the requester.

A stale tab cannot start.
A service developer who presses Start promotion after the approval lapsed sees the expiry copy and the promotion shown as expired.

Sync windows in cluster time.
Sync windows are weekly local-time ranges judged in the cluster's time zone, never the browser's or the server's.

Windows keep their wall-clock time.
Windows open at the same local time in the weeks either side of a clock change and follow the gap and overlap rule in Business rules, as listed by the openings endpoint.

Start only inside an open window.
A promotion enters applying only when the window check passes at that instant, and one that entered applying still finishes after its window closes.

Plan windows across time zones.
A platform engineer adds a window to a cluster, sees its next openings in cluster time and checks an instant, and a developer in another zone is then blocked or allowed by that cluster's clock.

Freeze policy versions.
Each promotion is judged by the freeze policy version in force at its request instant, so a new version affects only promotions requested from its effective instant on.

No lost freeze edits.
A new freeze policy version names the version it was based on, and one based on a version that is no longer the latest is refused.

Schedule a Black-Friday freeze.
A platform engineer schedules a freeze version for a future instant, and promotions requested either side of that instant show different policy versions and outcomes.

Break a freeze for an incident.
Only an on-call SRE with a recorded reason may move a window-blocked promotion on, and every release manager of the project receives one freeze-broken message.

Break a freeze from a phone.
An on-call SRE on a phone opens a blocked prod promotion from the vertical stage stack, breaks the freeze with a reason by touch, and sees it start applying.

Exact rollback.
A rollback starts a new promotion with the exact bundle digest and override set of the stage's last healthy promotion, read back from object storage, whatever the stage defaults are now.

Roll prod-us back at night.
An on-call SRE rolls a Degraded prod-us back to its last healthy revision from the evidence column and watches it reach Healthy.

Evidence snapshots.
Every promotion writes numbered evidence snapshots to object storage at the events listed in Services, and the download returns the latest stored snapshot byte for byte.

Secrets redacted in every copy.
Secret and sealed-value fields never appear in plain text in diffs, the evidence column, evidence snapshots, approval-link pages or any message.

Append-only promotion history.
Every promotion state change appends one history entry with from-state, to-state, instant and actor, and no entry is ever changed or removed.

Export an audit record.
A release manager downloads a finished prod promotion's evidence and finds who promoted which digest, under which policy version and window decision, with which approval.

Queued deliveries drain.
Evidence snapshots and messages that could not be delivered wait in the database and are delivered once each after their service returns, within the delay in Services and without a restart.

Delivery queue on screen.
The ledger strip shows storage and mail reachability and the queued upload and notice counts from the status endpoint.

Recover after storage and mail outages.
An on-call SRE sees queued uploads and notices counted while storage and mail are down and watches both counts fall to zero once they return.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` fields and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and the app starts from it alone.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` names every shipped package with its version and licence, where shipped packages are the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, and also lists the self-hosted fonts and icon set.
Every shipped package, font and icon set uses one of these licences: MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, or SIL OFL 1.1 for fonts.
The app uses no datastore other than the provided Postgres, MinIO and Mailpit: no SQLite, Redis, local files or in-memory stores as the record of state that must survive a restart.
The provided service configuration and its environment variable names stay as given.
`package-lock.json` is committed and `npm ci` installs from it.
Fonts, icons and scripts are served from the app's own origin, with no external network requests from the browser.
